Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-rays (Figures 1a-c) demonstrate a fracture of the left 8th rib (indicated by arrows in the lateral/oblique views and corresponding to the level of injury on the frontal view) which is directly adjacent to the area of pulmonary laceration/consolidation (indicated by the thick white arrow). This spatial relationship suggests the fractured rib caused the underlying lung injury.
